fact: Finance Minister Ngafuan cited reforms involving e-procurement among Liberia's partnerships and reforms, in a speech reported 2026-09-28.

The Liberian Observer reports the President formally launched the national e-GP system in February 2025, after a six-institution pilot; businesses register, bid and manage contracts on it, and Sierra Leone's procurement authority studied it in August 2026 as a working, deployed system.

PPCC says 56 government procurement entities are already onboarded onto the e-GP platform, as Phase II of its nationwide rollout began on 11 May 2026, with training on provider registration, annual procurement planning, e-notification, invitations and electronic bidding.

Tech Africa News reports the PPCC's e-GP system lets government institutions plan, advertise, evaluate and award procurement contracts digitally, replacing the manual process; more than 1,200 vendors are registered and the platform has raised more than US$400,000 in fees.
